messages:
anya: FYI support escalated a customer (cust-psi) complaining p99 ~1.8s on /v1/generate from EU clients since ~02:30 UTC. They sent traces showing spikes to 1.6-2.0s only for EU->APAC routed flows. Raising in eng-sre.
sanjay: Got it. Any repro steps from support? which regions, IPs, sample request IDs?
anya: Support attached these: region=eu-west-1, client IPs ~203.0.113.45/28 (VPN), sample request id: rqx-9a2f3. Also mentioned some latencies drop if client uses region=eu-central.
ops-bot: scheduled probes: eu-west1->api-redwood (tcp) p95=180ms, p99=320ms; eu-west1->edge-eu (#pop-14) TLS handshake p95=260ms p99=620ms. Probe timestamps 2026-03-16T02:41:00Z.
michael: I pulled p95 rollup for /v1/generate for EU clients: baseline pre-02:30 p95=180ms p99=350ms, post-02:30 p95=420ms p99=1.9s. Spike aligns w/ routing update around 02:28 UTC (gslb weight change).
beth: I grabbed tcpdump from pop-14 for one of the request ids. TLS handshake times look like:
```
ClientHello -> ServerHello elapsed 480ms
ServerHello -> Certificate elapsed 30ms
Certificate -> HandshakeComplete elapsed 1.1s
```
Meaning multiple retransmits/queueing during handshake.
sanjay: traceroute from EU client -> our pop-14 (edge-eu) attached:
```
1 10.0.0.1
2 198.51.100.4
3 198.51.100.9
4 203.0.113.254 (gslb-eu)  320 ms
5 198.51.100.33 edge-eu-pop14  340 ms
```
Looks like traffic was hairpinned via transit -> long RTT.
leo: Could be route shift to apac path via a peering change at 02:28. I see bgp weight update from our peering partner at that time in bgp-audit. Will check.
ops-bot: bgp-audit: partner-zz announced path preference change at 02:27:52 UTC for prefix 198.51.100.0/22. Affected POPs: pop-14, pop-22.
michael: Confirmed: config change we rolled 02:25 caused fallback to partner-zz in some AZs. Partner has longer transit to some EU VPN ranges -> handshake tail.
anya: Customer wants mitigation ASAP. Options: 1) force-route cust-psi to eu-central POPs (soft pin) 2) rollback routing change to previous peering preference 3) enable TCP keepalive TLS fast open? probably not helpful for in-progress sessions.
sanjay: Quick mitigation: add a per-customer routing rule to prefer internal backbone (pop-12) for IP block 203.0.113.0/28. I can push a canary ACL to edge-routes, then monitor p99. If that works, we can widen. Who can approve rollback of peering pref?
beth: Meanwhile, can we ask support to ask customer to test with header `Host: api.redwood.com` + `--resolve` to a closer pop for repro? Provide curl example:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:198.51.100.33 https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
This will let them validate if direct to pop reduces handshake tail.
leo: I can rollback peering pref with partner-zz but it needs network oncall approval due to flapping risk. Recommend canary route first.
anya: Sanjay please push the per-customer route canary to pop-14 only (ttl 30m). Post probe metrics.
sanjay: Doing now. Pushing route add for 203.0.113.0/28 -> prefer pop-12 next-hop via internal backbone (canary id canary-psi-pop14). Will notify when active.
ops-bot: canary canary-psi-pop14 activated at 2026-03-16T02:52:10Z on pop-14.
michael: Early numbers: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 190ms, p99 from 1.9s -> 380ms for the canaried IPs. Looks great.
anya: Good. Tell support we can keep canary for 2 hours then coordinate full roll. Also log RCA: bgp pref change -> partner-zz path introduced transit hairpin for some EU VPN ranges causing TLS handshake tails -> mitigation per-customer route and planned peering rollback if needed.
beth: Filing follow-up ticket for permanent routing policy + add automatic fallback to backbone when handshake tail >500ms for 5m.
leo: I'll coordinate partner-zz rollback window with network oncall @oncall-net for 03:30 UTC if needed.
sanjay: Closing loop with support now and attaching tcpdump, traceroute, canary metrics. :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks all. If we see recurrence open incident channel. :eyes:
